citations.assessment: This passage explicitly names bar Yosef. Other transmissions here use Rav Dimi without a patronym. The universal identification and proposed chronology are Heilprin’s.
Rashi gives both the literal gloss, possessor of a skull, and the idiomatic gloss, important man. The sugya gives the address to Dimi speaking to Abaye.
This is Heilprin’s lexical analogy with a head bearing no tefillin.
The passage describes Rabbi Yishmael’s scalp. Avodah Zarah preserves a parallel spelling.
The retrieved Arukh entry treats these related forms and glosses the address as a great man. The checked Rashi explicitly has the possessor-of-a-skull wording Heilprin gives here.
R. Yitzchak bar Yosef transmits R. Yochanan, then Abaye asks Dimi, who calls Abaye karkefana in the reply.
A distinct legal setting with a parallel exchange. The speaker transition immediately before the reply also names Abaye and Dimi.
Tosafot Eruvin identifies the head as Rabbah and preserves the chronological clause in brackets. Tosafot Yevamot gives the teacher reading and cites Ketubot.
This locus records the brothers’ message to Rabbah. Tosafot cites it in support of the travel claim; identify that as Tosafot’s interpretation.
Dimi tells Abaye what he heard and supplies the complete chain through Yirmeyah, Zeira, Chiyya bar Ashi and Rav.
Dimi reports a teaching and Abaye objects from the rule about a mixture of terumah.
Avya is absent because he was ill. Abaye questions him the next day. The source has no Dimi in this episode, as Heilprin himself explains in the linked Rav Avya notice.
Dimi transmits the teaching under Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yehudah Glustera. Compare Heilprin’s separate headword for Rabbi Yehudah Klustera and its explicit quotation.
Entry 1690 quotes exactly this Berakhot transmission and takes Glustera as Rabbi Yehudah’s appellation.
Dimi sends a retraction after going up to Nehardea. The prior report and the replacement both invoke Rabbi Yochanan.
The son of Rav Dimi bar Yosef mourns his child, saying the gestation was complete.
The checked Asheri text has bar Yitzchak parenthetically but still reads son of Dimi. The daughter reading reported by Heilprin remains uncollated.
The pointed entry explicitly gives Dimi’s father-in-law as an alternate reading to Rabbi Abba’s.
Rav Dimi gives the Rabbi Elazar transmission.
Dimi bar Yosef reports Rabbi Elazar on acquiring abandoned property.
Dimi bar Yosef reports Rabbi Elazar about retained movables.
Dimi transmits Rabbi Ammi transmitting Rabbi Chanina.
Dimi reports the episode involving Rabbi Ammi, Rabbi Assi and Rav Bibi.
Rav Dimi reports Zeiri reporting Rabbi Chanina.
Dimi gives the Chanina tradition, with a separate alternate attribution through Rabbi Zeira.
Dimi reports Rabbi Yochanan on an area less than four by four.
The sugya gives the same Rabbi Yochanan teaching through Dimi.
There are direct attestations of Rav Dimi reporting Rabbi Yonatan. This is one such comparison; the bare list does not select an individual teaching.
Dimi reports Rabbi Yannai on the dispute over the residents’ access.
Dimi gives Rabbi Yannai’s explanation regarding items that sprang from the altar fire.
The Bavli confirms this chain with the final designation רבינו, our master. Heilprin’s form רבי remains attributed to him.
This passage explicitly supplies the Merimar–Dimi chain. Identification with this headword remains qualified because the Bavli has the short name.
Dimi bar Yosef reports Rav Nachman’s explanation of the date.
Dimi bar Yosef questions Rav Nachman about a delegated slaughtering or separation of terumah.
The episode begins on 151a with Dimi’s sister. She comes before Rav Nachman, who summons Dimi. The threat is figurative in the text, and Heilprin renders it as a ban.
Dimi reports Rav Nachman bar Kohen’s interpretation of the king and the judge.
Berakhot explicitly has Rav Dimi bar Yosef reporting Rav. The nearby Zevachim locator supports the separate Rabbi transmission.
Dimi reports Rabbi about the sites of the divine presence.
Rashi explains the mnemonic by treating Dimi as first and Ravin as second. The underlying sequence likewise states that Dimi came before Ravin.
The checked text has Shmuel instructing Dimi bar Yosef to investigate. The Warsaw root’s anomalous initial yod remains visible.
Mar Shmuel instructs Dimi bar Yosef to startle the woman. The compiler infers studenthood from such reports, a stronger relation than the exchange establishes.
The verse provides both bedmi and the clause about being deprived of the rest of one’s years. The application to Dimi is attributed interpretation.
When Dimi went up he found Yirmeyah teaching. Rav Yosef’s objection precedes the encounter, but the compared passage does not describe Yirmeyah sending to Rav Yosef.
Heilprin’s Rabbah article quotes the same Tosafot and expressly asks how Tosafot derives an actual journey from the brothers’ invitation.
The Rav Avya article explicitly rejects Dimi’s participation and points to the corrected story in Berakhot 28b.
